data.description: Avionics equipment, IMA, software and bus attributes (ARP4754A / DO-178C / DO-254 / ARINC).
A port on a data bus: bus type and the address the bus uses (ARINC 429 label, AFDX virtual link, MIL-STD-1553 remote terminal).
Bus or signal type of the port
ARINC 429 label (octal) or ARINC 825 CAN identifier
A physical link between two ports: bus type, bandwidth, latency, cable length.
Bus or signal type of the link
Common attributes of avionics equipment (LRUs and IMA modules). Abstract: apply one of the derived stereotypes.
Hardware / item development assurance level (DO-254 / ARP4754A IDAL), A to E
Gateway or remote data concentrator between buses.
IMA line replaceable module (core processing or I/O module of an integrated modular avionics cabinet).
Robust ARINC 653 partitioning is claimed for this module, so partitions of different DAL may share it
ARINC 653 partition hosted by an IMA module.
Software level of the partition (DO-178C), A to E
Separation between the software items of this partition is claimed, so items of different DAL may share it
Item of the logical architecture with its assigned development assurance level.
Function / item development assurance level (ARP4754A FDAL / IDAL), A to E
ARP4754A / DO-178C attributes of a requirement.
Requirement level: system, item, software high-level (HLR) or low-level (LLR)
Development assurance level of what implements the requirement (DO-178C software level), A to E
Derived requirement: not traceable to a higher-level requirement; needs a rationale and feedback to the safety assessment
Verification method (superset of the generic field: also review and similarity)

elements.doc: ARP4754A system requirements of the avionics suite.
elements.name: SystemRequirements
Air data
elements.text: Air data for flight control, flight management and displays.

elements.name: Provide air data
elements.text: The air data system shall provide pressure altitude, computed airspeed, Mach number, vertical speed and total and static air temperature to the flight control, flight management and display systems at 20 Hz.

elements.name: Air data accuracy
elements.text: The air data system shall provide altitude to within 30 ft and airspeed to within 2 kt over the flight envelope.

elements.name: Detect erroneous air data
elements.text: An erroneous air data output shall be detected by comparison of two independent channels and annunciated within 1 second.

elements.name: Inertial reference
elements.text: Attitude, heading and inertial position.

elements.name: Provide attitude and heading
elements.text: The inertial reference system shall provide pitch, roll, heading, accelerations and position at 50 Hz.

elements.name: Attitude accuracy
elements.text: Pitch and roll shall be accurate to within 0.2 degrees (1 sigma).

elements.name: Navigation and altitude
elements.text: GNSS and radio altitude.

elements.name: Provide GNSS position
elements.text: The navigation system shall provide GNSS position and ground speed at 5 Hz.

elements.name: GNSS integrity monitoring
elements.text: The navigation system shall monitor the integrity of the GNSS position and annunciate loss of integrity within 10 seconds.

elements.name: Provide radio altitude
elements.text: The radio altimeter system shall provide radio altitude below 2500 ft at 20 Hz.

elements.name: Flight management and display
elements.text: Flight management and display requirements.

elements.name: Compute flight plan guidance
elements.text: The flight management function shall compute lateral and vertical guidance from the active flight plan at 5 Hz.

elements.name: Display primary flight data
elements.text: The display system shall present attitude, airspeed, altitude and heading on the PFD and the navigation data on the ND.

elements.name: Annunciate alerts
elements.text: The display system shall annunciate flight control and system alerts within 1 second of their detection.

elements.name: Flight control
elements.text: Fly-by-wire control laws and their monitoring.

elements.name: Compute control laws
elements.text: The flight control system shall compute the pitch and roll control laws and command the surface actuators at 40 Hz.

elements.name: Monitor the command lane
elements.text: Each flight control channel shall be monitored by a dissimilar monitor; the probability of an undetected erroneous surface command shall be less than 1E-9 per flight hour.

elements.name: Command latency
elements.text: The latency from sidestick movement to surface command shall not exceed 40 ms.

data.rationale: Introduced by the flight control design: the control laws need air data, so a defined reversion is required (fed back to the system safety assessment).

elements.name: Reversion on air data loss
elements.text: On loss of air data the flight control system shall revert to the direct law and annunciate the reversion.

elements.name: Platform
elements.text: Network, power and integration.

elements.name: Redundant networks
elements.text: Loss of either AFDX network shall not cause the loss of any function.

elements.name: Robust partitioning
elements.text: Partitions of different levels hosted in the IMA cabinet shall be robustly partitioned (ARINC 653).

elements.name: Redundant power
elements.text: Loss of one 28 VDC supply shall not cause the loss of any function.

elements.name: Maintenance logging
elements.text: The maintenance system shall record detected faults with time and flight phase.

elements.name: Environment
elements.text: Environment requirements.

elements.name: Environmental qualification
elements.text: The equipment shall be qualified to RTCA DO-160G for the categories of its equipment specification.

elements.doc: ARP4754A item requirements allocated to the equipment.
elements.name: ItemRequirements
Air data computer
elements.text: Air data computer requirements.

elements.name: ADC output rate
elements.text: The ADC shall transmit the air data labels at 20 Hz on ARINC 429 high speed.

elements.name: ADC reliability
elements.text: The ADC shall have an MTBF of at least 40000 hours.

elements.name: Flight control computer
elements.text: Flight control computer requirements.

elements.name: Fail-passive monitor
elements.text: On a mismatch between the command and monitor lanes the FCC shall remove the actuator engage discretes within 20 ms.

elements.name: Built-in test coverage
elements.text: Built-in test shall detect at least 98 percent of the failures that affect the control law computation.

elements.name: FCC execution frame
elements.text: The FCC shall complete the control law computation in a 25 ms frame.

elements.name: Network
elements.text: Network requirements.

elements.name: Switch latency
elements.text: The AFDX switch shall forward a frame within 150 microseconds.

elements.name: Concentrator conversion
elements.text: The RDC shall convert ARINC 429 labels to AFDX messages within 5 ms.

elements.name: Display and power
elements.text: Display and power requirements.

elements.name: Display refresh
elements.text: The display unit shall refresh the PFD symbology at 30 Hz or better.

elements.name: Power hold-up
elements.text: The power supply shall hold its output for 50 ms after loss of input power.

elements.name: Flight control software
elements.text: Flight control software requirements.

elements.name: Pitch control law
elements.text: The command lane shall compute the pitch demand from the sidestick, the air data and the inertial data every 25 ms.

elements.name: Invalid input handling
elements.text: The command lane shall treat an input as invalid when its status is not normal operation or its age exceeds 100 ms.

elements.name: Monitor comparison
elements.text: The monitor lane shall compare the commanded surface positions with its own computation and clear the engage discretes when they differ by more than the threshold.

elements.name: Flight management software
elements.text: Flight management software requirements.

elements.name: Guidance computation
elements.text: The navigation software shall compute the cross-track error and the track angle error every 200 ms.

elements.name: Software memory budget
elements.text: The flight management partition shall use no more than 48 MB of memory.

elements.name: Command lane algorithms
elements.text: Command lane algorithms requirements.

elements.name: Pitch law gain schedule
elements.text: The function pitch_demand shall interpolate the gain table linearly against computed airspeed.

elements.name: Output saturation
elements.text: The function pitch_demand shall saturate its result to the surface limits.

elements.name: Input age check
elements.text: The function input_valid shall reject an input older than 100 ms.

elements.name: Division guard
elements.text: The function gain_schedule shall not divide by a value with magnitude below 1E-6.

elements.name: Static memory
elements.text: The command lane source code shall use static allocation only.

Misleading airspeed and altitude; possible loss of control.
data.failure_condition: Erroneous air data on all channels, undetected

data.effect: Loss of primary attitude reference; large reduction in safety margins.
Cross-comparison annunciates the failure; crew selects the other source.
data.failure_condition: Erroneous attitude on one channel, detected

data.effect: Misleading height above ground during autoland; high crew workload.
Loss of height indication; crew uses barometric altitude.
Navigation continues on inertial reference.
Position error grows undetected; increased crew workload.
Crew navigates with the basic modes; significant workload increase.
Loss of electronic flight control; possible loss of control.
data.failure_condition: Loss of flight control computation, all channels

data.effect: Uncommanded surface movement; possible loss of control.
Latent: an erroneous command would no longer be detected.
Loss of control authority; possible loss of control.
Loss of primary flight data; crew uses the standby instruments.
Crew acts on wrong data; large reduction in safety margins.
Crew unaware of system failures; workload.
Loss of all avionics; only standby instruments remain.
Redundant supply carries the load.
Loss of communication between the avionics; reversion to direct modes.
The other network carries all traffic.
Fault history lost; troubleshooting takes longer.
